liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugar Magnolia** (2 reviews): The Sunshine Daydream section falls apart, typical of the era; the band struggled to exit it gracefully; Garcia is still using his wah-wah pedal on Sugar Magnolia [13][16]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): The show catches fire with Good Lovin' and Drums, followed by a nice Cumberland Blues [13]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Weir's vocals on the early-show Truckin' are singled out as something that must be heard [13]
- **Dancing In The Street** (1 review): Garcia stretches this tune out more than the reviewer has ever heard from him [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Six Days On The Road**: rare: 13 archived performances [24]
- **Superman**: rare: 10 archived performances [24]
- **Glendale Train**: rare: 13 archived performances [24]
- **Can't Pay The Price**: rare: 4 archived performances [24]
- **tmp**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 6 archived performances [24]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [24]
- **Hello Trouble**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Sweet Lovin' One**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-30.121126.sbd.deluca.digitalrbb.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 44 songs; 260 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd70-10-30.sbd.cotsman.20044.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 164 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound somewhat lacking for a soundboard source, though the show is tight; Sound quality drops noticeably between discs 1 and 2 and never recovers to first-disc quality; A high-pitched whine is noted about 1:02 into I Know You Rider [3][12][14]
- **gd1970-10-30.153005.sbd.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 27 songs; 166 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Some unintentional feedback was removed in this version; tape flip occurs in Me And My Uncle [4]
- **gd1970-10-30.153206.sbd.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac24**: soundboard; 27 songs; 163 min [6]
- **gd1970-10-30.early.sbd.lai.7466.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 59 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [9]. Said about its sound: Early show soundboard has vocals high in the mix; instruments get louder about a third of the way into Sugar Magnolia [16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended the first set as their first Dead show, and wished they had bought tickets for all four shows in the run [15]
- Reviewer wondered how the bearded guitarist could play with both the Dead and the NRPS; their dorm room housed out-of-town visitors [15]
- Reviewer is glad to hear Pigpen (Ron) in good form and apparently good health [19]
- Early show tape captures a microphone check exchange between stage voices before the music begins [21]
- Early show features NRPS as another act on the bill [1]
- Early show also features NRPS as another act [6]
- Reviewer calls the October 31st show the must-have, but says the two nights pair nicely [17]
- Reviewer suggests audience recordings with EQ as an alternative, citing 10/24 as a fantastic show [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-30.121126.sbd.deluca.digitalrbb.miller.flac16**: taped by Dat supplied By Dan De Luca Transferred By Digitalrbb; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch @7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Dat (Denon DTR 2000/48k) [1]. Also: Reel flip occurs during Me And My Uncle; a digital noise artifact is noted in another song [1]
- **gd70-10-30.sbd.cotsman.20044.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Complete early and late shows come via Jeff Cotsman; reel flip about 1:53 into Me & My Uncle [3]
- **gd1970-10-30.153005.sbd.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Gordon Healy; transferred by Jimmy Warburton, Matt Smith, SIRMick; source: SBD > Gordon Healy's Master Reel [4]
- **gd1970-10-30.153206.sbd.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by Matt Smith & SIRMick; source: SBD > Gordon Healy's Master Reel [6]. Also: Reel from Jimmy Warburton, transferred by Matt Smith; all tracks pitch corrected, 24-bit FLAC [6]
- **gd1970-10-30.early.sbd.lai.7466.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai and Wayne Gucwa; source: SDB>>MR>>PCM>>CD [9]
